cat > forgemyspec-board.yaml <<'EOF'
- id: R1
  status: doing
  title: "CSV Analytics Tool"

cat > forgemyspec-bundle/csv-analytics/spec.yaml <<'EOF'
version: "0.1"
title: "CSV Analytics Tool"
objective: "A single-file, stdlib-only Python module and CLI (csv_analytics.py) that reads CSV files, computes per-column statistics, filters rows, selects columns and exports a JSON report."
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: "Empty Python project; the deliverable is csv_analytics.py at the repository root with unittest tests under tests/. Python 3 standard library only."
  assumptions:
    - "The first CSV row is the header; column names are unique and non-empty."
    - "A column is numeric when every non-empty cell parses as a float; stats for non-numeric columns report count only, with min/max/mean/median/stdev as null."
    - "Empty cells are missing values and are excluded from count and from stats."
    - "stdev is the sample standard deviation (n-1); it is null when fewer than 2 values exist."
    - "Filter syntax is COLUMN OP VALUE with OP in ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=; numeric comparison when both sides parse as numbers, string comparison otherwise; multiple filters are ANDed."
    - "Stats are computed after filtering and column selection, over the remaining rows and columns."
    - "The CLI is: csv_analytics.py FILE [--filter EXPR]... [--columns A,B] [--output report.json]; without --output the JSON goes to stdout."
constraints:
  - "Python standard library only; no third-party packages."
  - "All code lives in the single file csv_analytics.py."
  - "No plotting, no database, no network access, no writing back to the CSV."
  - "No support for multiple input files in one report."
success_criteria:
  - "Per-column count, min, max, mean, median and stdev match values computed by hand on fixture CSVs."
  - "Filters and column selection change which rows and columns appear in the report."
  - "The JSON report is valid JSON and contains the stats per column."
  - "Bad input (missing file, unknown column, bad filter) exits with code 2 and a message on stderr."
hypotheses:
  - {id: h1, description: "For each numeric column the tool reports count, min, max, mean, median and sample stdev correctly.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h2, description: "Rows are filtered by column comparison expressions, combined with AND.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h3, description: "Only the selected columns appear in the output and in the stats.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h4, description: "The tool writes a valid JSON report with the stats per column to a file or stdout.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h5, description: "Invalid input is rejected with exit code 2 and a stderr message instead of a traceback.", confidence: 0.85}
required_evidence:
  - "unittest run output showing all tests in tests/ passing"
  - "gate report ending in RESULT: PASS"
  - "sample CLI run output on a fixture CSV showing the JSON report"
actions:
  - {id: a1, description: "Implement CSV reading and per-column stats in csv_analytics.py", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1]}
  - {id: a2, description: "Implement row filtering and column selection", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h2, h3]}
  - {id: a3, description: "Implement JSON report export and the CLI with error handling", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h4, h5]}
  - {id: a4, description: "Run the unit tests and the gate", type: validate, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5]}
decision_rules:
  - "If a behavior is not covered by an obligation, ask for a spec amendment before building it."
  - "If a test fails, fix the code, never the test, unless the spec is wrong; then amend the spec."
metadata:
  source_prompt: "Build a CSV Analytics Tool. Read CSV files, compute per-column stats (count, min, max, mean, median, stdev), filter rows, select columns, export JSON report. Single file csv_analytics.py, stdlib only."
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "per-column stats"
      - "filter rows"
      - "select columns"
      - "export JSON report"
      - "single file csv_analytics.py"
      - "stdlib only"
formal:
  module: CsvAnalytics
  obligations:
    - id: column_stats
      kind: boundary
      statement: "For each numeric column the report has count, min, max, mean, median and sample stdev matching hand-computed values."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["per-column stats"]
      test: "test_csv_analytics.StatsTests.test_numeric_column_stats"
    - id: filter_rows
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Filter expressions keep only matching rows; several filters are ANDed."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["filter rows"]
      test: "test_csv_analytics.FilterTests.test_filters_are_anded"
    - id: select_columns
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Only the selected columns appear in the report; an unknown column exits 2."
      hypotheses: [h3, h5]
      must_include: ["select columns"]
      test: "test_csv_analytics.SelectTests.test_selected_columns_only"
    - id: json_report
      kind: boundary
      statement: "The CLI writes a valid JSON report with per-column stats to --output or stdout."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["export JSON report"]
      test: "test_csv_analytics.ReportTests.test_json_report_written"
    - id: bad_input
      kind: boundary
      statement: "A missing file or a malformed filter exits 2 with a stderr message and no traceback."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["export JSON report"]
      test: "test_csv_analytics.ErrorTests.test_bad_input_exits_2"
    - id: single_file_stdlib
      kind: boundary
      statement: "csv_analytics.py imports only standard library modules and lives in one file."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["single file csv_analytics.py", "stdlib only"]
      test: "test_csv_analytics.StructureTests.test_stdlib_only_single_file"
scope:
  paths: ["csv_analytics.py", "tests/**"]
  tests: tests
  pythonpath: ["."]
EOF
export PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness
python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/csv-analytics/spec.yaml --formal && python3 -m forgemyspec package forgemyspec-bundle/csv-analytics/spec.yaml

result:
The spec is written and passes lint at 100/100, but I need your approval before I can write any code. The bundle is `forgemyspec-bundle/csv-analytics/spec.yaml`. It is spec-only: every check is a Python boundary test, with no Dafny proofs.

**What you'd be approving**
- **Deliverable:** one file, `csv_analytics.py`, using only the standard library. It works as a module and as a CLI: `csv_analytics.py FILE [--filter EXPR]... [--columns A,B] [--output report.json]`. Without `--output`, the JSON goes to stdout.
- **Stats:** each numeric column gets count, min, max, mean, median and sample stdev.
- **Filters and columns:** filters are ANDed. Stats are computed after filtering and column selection.
- **Errors:** a missing file, unknown column or bad filter exits with code 2 and a message on stderr.

**Assumptions I made, which you should check**
- The first row of the CSV is the header.
- A column is numeric only if every non-empty cell parses as a float. A non-numeric column reports count only, and its other stats are null.
- Empty cells are missing values and are left out of count and stats.
- stdev uses n−1, and is null when a column has fewer than 2 values.
- A filter is `COLUMN OP VALUE`, with OP one of `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`. It compares as numbers when both sides parse as numbers, and as strings otherwise.

**Boundary tests (one per obligation)**

| Obligation | What the test checks |
|---|---|
| `column_stats` | Stats match hand-computed values. |
| `filter_rows` | Several filters are ANDed. |
| `select_columns` | Only the chosen columns appear, and an unknown column exits 2. |
| `json_report` | Valid JSON is written to `--output` or stdout. |
| `bad_input` | A missing file or bad filter exits 2 with no traceback. |
| `single_file_stdlib` | Only standard-library imports, in one file. |

To approve, type this code in the chat: **LTRLUT**
